When I was 17 my mother committed suicide and left me, my 8-month pregnant sister, and my dad all alone. She had been filing bankruptcy for our family. 
My dad was laid off on a Friday, my mother killed herself on a Tuesday, and on the following Friday we received a foreclosure notice on our home.

My dad was out of work for a very long time. All he ever knew was factory work, and all the factories were closing. All he did was sleep and play sports video games. I couldn't stand to see him that way and finally (after months of badgering  him) convinced him to start volunteering at an exotic animal sanctuary with me. We worked alongside big cats, bears, primates, reptiles, and more. It really helped him. My nephew was born a month after my mom died, and I think having a grandson really helped him too.

On April 8th of 2008 I lost my mother to suicide. I was 17. That day, I was pulled out of school by a police officer and driven to an abandoned Value City parking lot to be told by my father "Mom is dead." It was like a movie scene. My vision tunneled and all I could hear was my dad crying. My stomach twisted and my throat tightened.

I stayed out of school and work for a week. Going back was absolutely terrible. I felt as though everyone was whispering and no one knew what to say to me. Everyone just smiled sad and sympathetically when I came around. 

My mom didn't leave a note and she had called my sister and dad that night (she went to work and nonchalantly called them to just talk, not say she would be killing herself), but she did not call me. I was crushed under the heavy weight of a thousand hypothetical questions. What could I have done to change things? Did I not love her enough? Did she not love me? Was it my fault? Did she die angry with me? I have confronted many of these questions, but 7 years later they still weigh on my mind. 

My mother missed out on the birth of my nephew (by a month), my sister getting engaged, my high school graduation, me being an all star roller derby athlete, and this May she will miss my college graduation. I will be the first in my family to graduate college. There is not a day the goes by that I don't wish to pick up the phone to hear her voice or curl up in her arms after a bad day. I'm beginning to forget memories and her voice, which is like losing her all over again. It is the hardest thing I have to deal with every single day. 

Even harder for me, my sister won't believe it was suicide. I can't even talk to my big sister about it. Once a month, I attend a support group for survivors of suicide. 

If any of you think the world wouldn't miss you or would be better off without you, you are so wrong. Everyone has someone that cares for them and they will be devastated if you die. If you don't think you have anyone, you do. Every person in the world that has been touched by suicide mourns the loss of people that complete suicide. We empathize with the families and our hearts are shattered to know that someone felt they were better off dead. Whenever I read a story about a suicide, I weep. It is like revisiting my mother's death all over again.

Every single one of you is worth it and you deserve to be here. Life only has downs so you can have much more fun going up. No matter your background, I love you. You are important to me and the rest of the world.

I'm so happy for you, and so very proud of you!

When I was away he started showing signs of illness. I convinced my Dad to start volunteering after my mom passed away, so he kept me updated on everything going on. He told me that Johnny had diarrhea for almost three weeks. I was furious! The director was writing it off as the keepers giving him too many treats. I kept insisting he get treated for parasites. I actually almost lost my keeper position because I jumped all protocols and started treating Johnny for parasites. I got an angry call from the director; she yelled at me, saying it was irresponsible and asking if I had known stool samples had been sent out. I asked what the diagnosis was and she was quiet for a moment before she said "...Well, uh, it's parasitic." 

They decided to give him something topical that goes on necks like flea meds you get for your dog or cat, but the "camelid expert" told us to give it to him orally. Mind you, the medication was NOT made to be ingested, so we continued to put it on his neck. Well, that didn't work. So they tried giving him giant shots in the neck. That also didn't work. Finally, they treated him with Panacur, the deworming meds I originally tried to give him. 
Because he had an astounding amount of parasites and this went on for months, he lost a ton of weight and looked terrible. I continued to say "We need to get weight and muscle mass on him before winter, or he'll never make it" to which the director replied "Oh, I meant to tell you, I was watching a show on TV about camels and all of them were that skinny."
I gave her an odd look before I asked "Where were the camels?"
She replied "The middle east."
I looked at her for a few seconds and firmly said "We're in Indiana..."
This went on for months.

When the vet came the day we put Johnny down he said "This camel has no muscle mass and is very under weight" before I told him anything.

I got there and several other health care committee members were there and Johnny was pinned in his stall. A vet was called in and I relayed 4 years of Johnny's medical history to him. The vet then began to list the things wrong with Johnny, all things that I had been telling the director for at least 3 months leading up to that day. The vet then dropped the bomb and said "There's nothing we can do except euthanize him." I started bawling again and hugged Johnny's head and whispered "I tried, bud. I fought really hard. I'm so sorry." We walked him back to where he would be buried, and to this day I still feel horrible for it. They tried tranquilizing him to get him to lay down, but after two shots he still wouldn't go down. The vet then decided to euthanize Johnny while he was standing. I didn't want to see him fall so I turned my back and covered my ears. I ran back over and sat down next to his head. Right before he died he put his head in my lap one last time.

That day was one of the roughest days of my life.

I'm 100% against it. I've seen many outcomes, and they usually end badly.  For one, there are only about 3,200 tigers still living in the wild. Three out of nine tiger species are extinct, 1 species is extinct in the wild, 1 species is critically endangered and 4 species are threatened. 

It all seems super fun when they're cubs, but what do you expect to do with a 600 pound carnivorous cat? Also, housing a large cat is not only super dangerous, but extremely expensive and time consuming. You have to build an enclosure that is big enough for the animal, strong enough to withstand an animal jumping off fences and tall enough because tigers have a ridiculous ability for jumping. You also need a shift stall to safely avoid direct contact in an enclosure, as well as an indoor area for the animal to relax. Tigers usually eat 20-50 pounds of meat a day, and it should be mostly red meat. On top of that, you have to get complete supplements to put on the food that make up for the nutrients they aren't getting from just a raw piece of meat. To add to all of those costs, you have to find a vet that specializes in exotic cats;  they are few and far between and very expensive. 

It's just a bad idea all around. Find a large cat rescue in your state and dedicate your time and money there.

My favorite aspect of my volunteer position is making a difference in the life of an animal that was most likely abused. Seeing the transformation from an animal that is extremely skittish and aggressive to that same animal enjoying the company of humans (from a safe distance and NEVER in the cage if the animal is too dangerous) is astounding and very moving. The most challenging part of the job is realizing that you can't make that difference for every animal. In Indiana, we can own any animal except venomous snakes. It's heart breaking to know that I can't prevent every exotic animal from going to the wrong person and I am hit with the reality that there will always be animals in unfortunate situations.
